title: Camp 2 close: the tabernacle (Exodus 35–40)
hookLine: Exodus ends with a portable dwelling built from everyone's gifts
last: THE BROKEN TABLETS WERE KEPT TOO.

cards: A potluck is a strange kind of feast: somebody brings the table, somebody brings the chairs, and somebody brings the extension cord nobody remembered. It belongs to everyone because everyone brought a piece.
The book of Exodus could have ended with thunder on the mountain. It doesn't. Its last chapters are about a building project in the desert: a tent, made of gifts, that could be folded up and carried.

teach.b: The instruction comes in one line, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation: "And let them make Me a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them." Later commentators pointed out that it doesn't say in it.
It says among them. The building is for the people.
Moses asks for gifts from everyone whose heart moves them: gold, silver, copper, blue and purple and scarlet yarn, linen, goats' hair, wood, oil, spices. Women spin the goats' hair.
The women who served at the tent's entrance give their copper mirrors for the washing basin. An artist named Bezalel, filled, the text says, with wisdom and skill, leads the work.
Then something happens that fundraisers can only dream of: the people bring too much. The craftsmen tell Moses, and Moses sends word through the camp to stop giving.
The word mishkan comes from the root shachan, to dwell, the same root as Shekhinah, the word Jews use for God's presence dwelling close by.
And Exodus ends with that presence arriving: a cloud covers the tent, "and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle." When the cloud lifted, the people traveled. When it stayed, they stayed.

So camp two ends here, after seventy-five days of stories: the voice at the beginning, the garden, Cain and Abel, Noah and the rainbow, Babel, Abraham going forth, Sarah laughing, Jacob wrestling, Joseph and his brothers, the midwives, the bush, the plagues, the sea, the mountain, the calf.
It started with a world made by words.

teach.h: THAT I MAY DWELL AMONG THEM.
teach.b: It ends with people building a small place for God to live among them, out of whatever they had.

how: The building of the mishkan is read in synagogue in the last portions of Exodus, and many Jews see each synagogue and each home table as a small sanctuary in its line.

games.q: you're one of the craftsmen. the people keep bringing gold, yarn and wood, far more than the plan needs. what do you do?
o: take it all and build bigger.
tell Moses there's more than enough.
quietly store the extra for later.
games.why: the craftsmen tell Moses the people bring more than enough, and Moses sends word through the camp to stop giving.

practice: Let one story from this camp stay with you. Then think of something shared you belong to: a family, a building, a team, a congregation, a street.
Choose one small thing you could bring to it, an hour, a skill, a dish, a thank-you note, a few dollars, the way the people chose their gifts: because your heart moved you.

wordCard.voice: Mishkan. The dwelling, the tabernacle, a portable home for God's presence, built from everyone's gifts. Camp two, complete.

orig.note: Hebrew: dwelling, from shachan, to dwell, the root of Shekhinah, God's presence.

carryVoice: Your line: build a place, presence comes. Tomorrow camp three begins: the practices, starting with Shabbat. That's day ninety-six.
